63: // diff compares two multi-line strings and returns a helpful comment
64: func diff(got, want string) string {
65: 	g := strings.Split(got, "\n")
66: 	w := strings.Split(want, "\n")
67: 	for i := 0; ; i++ {
68: 		switch {
69: 		case i < len(g) && i < len(w):
70: 			if g[i] == w[i] {
71: 				continue
72: 			}
73: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- first difference in line %d:\n"+
74: 				"-- got : %q\n-- want: %q\n", i+1, g[i], w[i])
75: 		case i < len(g):
76: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d extra lines after line %d:\n"+
77: 				"-- first extra line: %q\n", len(g)-len(w), i, g[i])
78: 		case i < len(w):
79: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d correct lines, want %d more lines:\n"+
80: 				"-- want next: %q\n", i, len(w)-i, w[i])
81: 		default:
82: 			return "no differences found"
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: }

I found a bug: I was using `animals[v]` (the current animal) for all the chain lines, but in each chain line, the animal that gets swallowed should be the animal in the chain that is one step above the one being caught. In other words, if k is the index of the animal being caught, then the one doing the swallowing is animals[k+1].

Fix: `lines = append(lines, "She swallowed the "+animals[k+1]+" to catch the "+animals[k]+catchSuffix[k]+".")`
The chain lines must reference each animal in the chain (the one swallowed is the next animal up), not repeat the verse's animal. Fixing:

input.oldString: lines = append(lines, "She swallowed the "+animals[v]+" to catch the "+animals[k]+catchSuffix[k]+".")
input.newString: lines = append(lines, "She swallowed the "+animals[k+1]+" to catch the "+animals[k]+catchSuffix[k]+".")

content.text: Wait — for verse v, the chain starts from animals[v] catching animals[v-1]. In my loop, when k = v-1, animals[k+1] = animals[v]. Correct.
All tests pass, and vet is clean too.

All tests pass. The implementation in `food_chain.go` is fully algorithmic:

- **`animals`** — 1-based slice of the eight animals in order (fly → horse).
- **`comments`** — map of verse number → the second line (the "How absurd..." / "She's dead, of course!" style comment); the fly verse has none.
- **`catchSuffix`** — map adding "that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her" only to the spider when it appears as the caught animal.
- **`Verse(v)`** — first line, optional comment, then walks the chain downward (each animal catching the previous one) plus the refrain, joined with newlines. Verse 8 (horse) has no chain or refrain.
- **`Verses(start, end)`** / **`Song()`** — join verses with blank lines; `Song()` is `Verses(1, 8)`.

One bug was caught on the first run: the chain lines initially repeated the verse's animal; each line must name the animal one step up in the chain (`animals[k+1]` catches `animals[k]`). `go test ./...` and `go vet` are clean, and `food_chain_test.go` was not modified.
